newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Seven firms seek stake in Kazakh telecoms monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Seven firms seek stake in Kazakh telecoms monopoly.

text.p: Seven companies are seeking to buy a 40 percent stake in Kazakh telecoms monopoly NAK Kazakhtelekom, up from four announced earlier, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.

Andar Shukputov, deputy head of the ministry's property department, said the number of the participants of the tender wishing for a stake in Kazakhtelekom had risen after the government extended the deadline to March 21 from March 15.

He said bidders were Germany's Siemens AG, Alcatel Alsthom SA unit Alcatel Sel AG, Korea's Daewoo Corp and Hanwha Corp, Malaysia's Usaha Tegas Sdn Bnd and Kazakhstan's Asset Management Ltd, and Kaztel Investment Group which is registered in the British Virgin Islands.

"The bids will be passed on to the inter-ministerial tender commission headed by (deputy prime minister and finance minister) Alexander Pavlov," Shukputov told reporters and government officials as he opened envelopes with the bids.
Pavlov's commission will select one or two companies which will have an exclusive right to negotiate directly with the government on the contract.

Kazakhtelekom chairman Serik Burkitbayev, present as the envelopes were opened, refused to comment further on the tender, which was announced in January after a government deal with Germany's Deutche Telekom AG fell through.
Burkitbayev told Reuters in an interview last week he expected the winner of the tender would be named in April.
He said Kazakhtelekom, where 90 percent of shares are state-owned and 10 percent belong to its employees, needed investment of around 1.5 billion marks.

Kazakhtelekom wants an investor to share responsibility for debts of 420 million marks for a credit granted in 1992 by Germany's investment agency Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau which must be repaid by 2004.
The monopoly wants to bring the number of telephone lines in the Central Asian state with a population of 16.9 million people to five million from 2.1 million today.
Kazakhstan also wants to use its geographical position right in the centre of Eurasia efficiently to become a communications hub linking Europe and Asia.
